q: How do I fix rounded shoulders?
a: Start with wall angels and chin tucks, 2 sets of 10 every day, and set a posture check every few hours. Strengthening your upper back matters more than stretching alone. Open Posture exercises to follow along with the figure, and re-check with the body scan in two weeks.

q: What should I eat to lose weight on a veg diet?
a: Keep most plates built around protein and vegetables: moong chilla or poha with peanuts for breakfast, dal with roti and sabzi for lunch, sundal as a snack, and a lighter paneer or tofu dinner. Swap fried snacks for roasted ones and keep water up. Your Diet & body plan sets the portions for your goal.

q: I am a beginner — where do I start with Kalaripayattu?
a: Begin with meippayattu basics: hip and hamstring warm-ups, then slow leg swings and the elephant and lion stances (vadivu), holding each and breathing through the nose. Practise barefoot on a non-slip floor, a few minutes a day. Partner and weapon work belongs with a qualified teacher.

q: What makes clothes look good on me?
a: Fit matters most: shoulder seams at your shoulder edge, sleeves ending at the wrist bone and trousers that skim rather than cling or sag. A simple tailor adjustment often beats buying something new.

q: How do I know if I'm warm or cool toned?
a: Look at your wrist veins in daylight: greenish suggests warm, blue or purple suggests cool, a mix suggests neutral. Gold jewellery flattering you more hints warm; silver hints cool. The app's colour check walks you through it.

q: What is a simple daily skincare routine?
a: Morning: gentle cleanser, moisturiser, sunscreen (SPF 30+). Night: cleanse to remove dirt and sunscreen, then moisturise. Add one targeted product (like vitamin C or a retinoid) only once your skin is used to the basics.

q: How do I make makeup last in heat?
a: Use a light, mattifying moisturiser, thin layers, cream products set with a little powder, and a setting spray. Carry blotting papers instead of adding more powder.
